sheets.heading: Major Rivers
sheets.text:
Major Rivers

Africa • Nile: White Nile (Lake Victoria) + Blue Nile (Lake Tana, Ethiopia) meet at Khartoum

(Sudan) → Mediterranean Sea.

o 11 basin countries. Chad is not in the Nile basin (frequent trap). o “Egypt is the Gift of the Nile”.

• Congo (Zaire): Deepest river, crosses Equator twice, drains into Atlantic. Congo Basin = world’s 2nd largest tropical rainforest + largest tropical peatland.

• Zambezi: Victoria Falls; drains into Indian Ocean.

• Niger: West Africa; inland delta.

• Limpopo: Crosses Tropic of Capricorn twice.

South America

• Amazon: Largest by discharge & drainage area. Origin in Andes (Peru). Flows through Brazil mainly → Atlan c.

• Orinoco: Venezuela/Colombia.

• Parana–Paraguay: Important for Southern Cone.

North America

• Mississippi–Missouri: Combined system is very long. Bird’s-foot delta. Source of Mississippi is Lake Itasca.

• Colorado: Grand Canyon (not on Mississippi).

• St. Lawrence: Connects Great Lakes to Atlantic.

Asia • Yangtze: Longest in Asia; Three Gorges Dam (world’s largest HEP).

• Yellow River (Huang He): China’s sorrow (heavy silt).

• Mekong: Does not flow through Malaysia. Drains into South China Sea (not Andaman Sea).

• Amur: Far East Russia/China.

• Lena, Yenisei, Ob: Siberian rivers → Arc c Ocean.

• Volga: Europe’s longest; drains into Caspian Sea (endorrheic).

• Tigris–Euphrates: Mesopotamia; Persian Gulf.

Europe

• Danube: Most international (10 countries) → Black Sea.

• Rhine: Rift valley; important waterway.

• Thames: North Sea (not Irish Sea – UPSC trap).

• Dnieper: Black Sea. Sea/Ocean Major Rivers

• Caspian Sea: Largest inland sea/lake; 5 bordering countries (Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, Azerbaijan). Armenia does not border it.

• Black Sea: Inland sea connected to Mediterranean; Croatia does not border it.

• Red Sea: Receives very little precipitation; no rivers flow into it

• Aral Sea: Has shrunk immensely due to human activities (irrigation diversions)

• Mediterranean Sea: Borders Morocco (among North African countries).

• Sequence (West to East): Mediterranean → Black Sea → Caspian Sea → Aral Sea.

• Canada is the largest producer and exporter of softwood timber and wood pulp.

• Tropical rainforest soil is nutrient-poor; once cleared, regeneration is slow.

• Dense forests are mostly found near the equator.
